purpose: Separate exact-species evidence from related Malva and human-food evidence before any tortoise feeding verdict is considered.

evidence.citation: Kojima T, Kishi M, Sekita S, Satake M. Origin of sennosides in health teas including Malva leaves. 2001.
evidence.method: thin-layer chromatography and high-performance liquid chromatography
evidence.result: Sennosides A and B were not detected in M. verticillata leaves in the study; sennosides in sampled health teas were traced to senna material.
evidence.supports: A narrow negative finding for sennosides A/B in tested M. verticillata leaves.
evidence.does_not_support: Whole-plant tortoise safety, feeding role, feeding frequency, nitrate safety, oxalate safety, or nutritional completeness.

evidence.study_type: chemical profiling and in-vitro antioxidant assay
evidence.result: Chemical constituents and phenolic content were characterized in extracts; leaves showed the highest reported total phenolic content among tested parts.
evidence.does_not_support: Tortoise feeding safety, captive diet percentage, oxalate or nitrate burden.

evidence.study_type: rat pharmacology with methanolic leaf extract
evidence.result: Screening reported alkaloids, saponins, phenols, flavonoids, ash and tannins in the methanolic extract.
evidence.supports: Presence of broad phytochemical classes in the tested extract.
evidence.does_not_support: Concentration in fresh edible leaves, tortoise toxicity, or feeding recommendation.

evidence.supports: Malva parviflora is documented in a wild T. g. graeca diet in Morocco.
evidence.does_not_support: Malva verticillata safety or a captive feeding percentage for T. g. ibera.

canonical_interpretation.identity: Korean cultivated 아욱 can be mapped to Malva verticillata L. when the crop identity is established.
canonical_interpretation.feeding_verdict: Do not unlock or upgrade solely from this evidence set.
canonical_interpretation.applicability: plant_only plus related-species feeding context; no verified exact T. g. ibera feeding evidence in this pass.
canonical_interpretation.public_wording_guardrail: State what is known and unknown. Do not call it staple, daily food, unlimited food, or unsafe based on the evidence above.
